sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

How far the typical project's effect applies to this charity's work
rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small nuclear project applies to the work Ploughshares pays for. Most grants fund typical field work (arms-control research and advocacy at the Arms Control Association, FAS, the Stimson Center, RAND and Carnegie; congressional advocacy by FCNL and Win Without War; Track 2 on Korea by the Quincy Institute and the National Committee on North Korea), and a funder that has picked grantees for 44 years may choose better than average. Below a typical project: about $0.5M of the $3.1M (WASL's peacebuilding, the Women of the Middle East Network, J Street, NIAC Action, Win Without War) is diplomacy and war prevention only partly aimed at nuclear risk, about $0.17M (Marshallese education, the Nuclear Truth Project, RECA advocacy, Kiribati delegates) is justice for those harmed by past testing, and much of Ploughshares' own work is communications and convening, whose path to the risk is longest. Net 0.65, our judgment, 0.25 to 1.1; below NTI's 0.8, which runs its own diplomacy with senior officials.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: The share of the work no one else would have done now: nuclear threat reduction is a small field whose funding is shrinking (MacArthur left in 2021; the annual report, p. 44: "philanthropic support for nuclear threat reduction is declining sector-wide"), so grantees would mostly not replace a Ploughshares grant soon, and few others run the field's coalitions; but other funders (Longview, Carnegie Corporation, Rockefeller Brothers Fund, Open Society) fund many of the same groups. Our judgment, 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9), as for NTI; that the work would have come years later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: Ploughshares' share of the resources behind the outcome: a grant buys its own share of a grantee's work (the cut is per dollar, so co-funders' dollars are already left out), but its coalitions (the Stop the New Nuclear Arms Race Roundtable, the Iran coalition, the North Korea working group, Aligning Action) and the March 2025 Hill day run on about 30 partners' staff time it doesn't pay for. Our judgment, 0.85 (0.6 to 1), as for NTI.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether other funders of nuclear work would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.ploughshares_fund (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of Ploughshares' or its grantees' work on the risk is measured; the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted: work against a limited nuclear war or a single detonation (the testing and Korea work), which kills far fewer than 10% of people and has no shared forecast (nuclear_smaller_per_year 0); grants against conventional war (diplomacy with Iran in the year of the June 2025 strikes); and the compensation and recognition won for people harmed by testing (the RECA expansion a grantee pushed for, a transfer within the US whose net gain after its cost to taxpayers is small). 10% (0 to 30%) of the modelled value, our judgment, as for NTI.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: A typical project's chance of backfiring is already in the shared cut per dollar (Rethink Priorities' backfire step). Ploughshares' grants fund policy, advocacy and education, which can't speed up any capability. 0, down to −5%, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): advocacy for restraint and disarmament could, some argue, weaken deterrence or provoke a backlash, and alarming public messages can feed fatalism (the reason for Ploughshares' narrative work); none is shown to happen. 0, down to −5%, our judgment.
